Iuppiter (not in slab word list; supplied by reader)

cognate: Gk Ζεύς = Ved. dyáuḥ (dyú-/div-) = Lat. Iu- (Iou-) < *dyḗws; Gk πατήρ = Ved. pitā́ = Lat. -piter/pater < *ph₂tḗr
drift_or_renewal: none in the lexemes; Latin has univerbated the phrase into one name (Iuppiter < voc. *dyeu-pater), with the inflected oblique built on Iou- (Ioui in the same Cato passages); Greek and Vedic keep two words, freely separable (Ζεὺς ὀμώμοται πατήρ; dyaur naḥ pitā)
shared_syntax: divine name *dyēus + apposed *ph₂tēr naming the same referent (nominative-appositive in Greek and Vedic, vocative-derived compound in Latin); Vedic and Greek allow a word between the two members
context: All anchors are speech-acts addressed to or invoking the sky-god: Rhesus 816 an oath ('Zeus the father has been sworn by'); AVŚ 6.120 an expiatory prayer in which dyaur naḥ pitā is paired with bhūmir mātā in the preceding line (the sky-father / earth-mother couple, also RV 1.89.4, 1.191.6, 6.51.5); Cato Agr. 132 and 134 sacrificial prayers (Iupiter dapalis macte ... esto; Iupiter macte isto ferto esto), where the same 'god + pater' vocative pattern recurs with Mars pater and Iane pater. Same referent, same title, same ritual-verbal setting in three branches; the epithet is not generic language (no other god is systematically 'X father' in all three) and the Latin fossilisation shows it was a fixed formula before Italic.
phrase: *dyēus ph₂tēr 'Father Sky': Ζεὺς ... πατήρ ~ dyaur ... pitā ~ Iupiter

cognate: Gk εὐρύς = Ved. urú- < *h₁wérHus 'wide'; Gk πόντος = Ved. pánthā-/path- < *póntoh₁s 'path, passage'
drift_or_renewal: drift of the noun: *póntoh₁s 'way, passage' is 'path' in Vedic (and Slavic путь, cf. the route/passage sense in lav 7.1, 235.14 in this slab) but 'open sea' in Greek, i.e. the sea as the way to be crossed; the adjective is unchanged
shared_syntax: attributive adjective *h₁wérus + noun *póntoh₁s, same case agreement, typically object or locative of a verb of travelling (Gk ἐπιπλὼς εὐρέα πόντον, περήσαμεν εὐρέα πόντον; Ved. pathā́ urúṇā ... asarji, urúm ... pánthām ánvetavaí, uraú pathí ... tasthúḥ)
context: Lead anchor is Hdt 2.116.3, which quotes Il. 6.291 verbatim (Paris 'sailing over the wide pontos'); Hdt 4.86.3 has only εὐρύτατον predicated of the Pontus with a partitive genitive (weak, listed for completeness). In Vedic the wide path is the road travelled by the sun, gods, chariot or the dakṣiṇā; in Greek the wide pontos is the sea-road travelled by ships. In both the phrase is a formula: Homeric line-end εὐρέα πόντον / εὐρέι πόντῳ (9 lines in the AGDT Homer), Vedic urú- + pánthā- in 6 pādas plus stanza-level RV 1.24.8, 5.47.2. Caveat: εὐρύς is a generic Greek sea-epithet (εὐρέα κόλπον, εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης), so the Greek half alone could be independent; the case rests on the exact double cognation plus the traversal context explaining the noun's drift.
phrase: *h₁wérus póntoh₁s 'wide way': εὐρέα πόντον ~ urúḥ pánthāḥ

support.locus: Il. 6.264; Il. 1.357; Il. 18.35; Od. 6.30 (33 Homeric lines with πότνια + μήτηρ)
RV: 0 pādas/stanzas with mātár- + pátnī-; AV (DCS): only AVŚ 7.6.3

cognate: Gk πότνια = Ved. pátnī- < *pótnih₂ 'mistress'; Gk μήτηρ = Ved. mātár- < *méh₂tēr
drift_or_renewal: none in form; Ved. pátnī- has narrowed to 'wife, lady' and here heads a genitive (ṛtasya patnī), Gk πότνια is an honorific epithet
shared_syntax: weak: in Greek πότνια is an attributive/vocative epithet of μήτηρ ('lady mother'); in AVŚ 7.6.3 mātaraṃ (+ gen. suvratānām) and patnīm (+ gen. ṛtasya) are two separate appositions to the same goddess (Aditi), not epithet + noun
context: Both are invocations of a divine mother: Ion 410 'ὦ πότνια Φοίβου μῆτερ' to Leto, mother of Apollo; AVŚ 7.6.3 calling on Aditi as 'mother of the well-ruling [Ādityas], mistress of ṛta'; IA 1487 addresses Iphigenia's mother. The Vedic pairing is a single instance (0 in RV) and the syntax differs, so this is at best a weak echo of a possible *pótnih₂ + *méh₂tēr address to a divine mother; filed for completeness, not as a secure formula.

note: All 216 bundles read. Mostly Herodotus/Euripides pivots against Cato, Lucretius, Plautus, AV, OE, ORu prose: little inherited. Claims: Dyēus ph₂tēr (high), εὐρὺς πόντος ~ urú pánthā (medium), πότνια μήτηρ ~ mātṛ/patnī (low). Considered and rejected: στέγη δόμων ~ tecta domorum (post-Homeric, generic), βρέμω+ἅλς ~ brim+sealt (structure differs, generic), λήγω ὕπνου ~ languere sopore (different sense), bones/flesh, snow/winter, locked doors (content-determined).
